Richard Dawkins coined the term 'meme' in 1976. It is a shortening of mīmēma, or imitated thing, coming from the Greek μιμεῖσθαι, to imitate. Its definition, according to the Merriam-Webster dictionary is 'an idea, behavior, style, or usage that spreads from person to person within a culture'.

This is what reddit's comments section was in general: a collection of ideas generated within the site that spread from user to user. Someone posted a 'successful' or 'witty' comment which was highly upvoted. Hours later (in occasions, minutes later) there were people imitating the same comment. The original comment became an imitated thing, it became a meme. This is something you could see in most askreddit threads, where some user made a reference to one of the most upvoted comments of the thread. The obliged comment 'this thread has gone meta' ensued, giving rise to a new meme, that, like all reddit's memes, would eventually be abused and over-used. The problem with these memes in reddit is that people understand the reference to the original comment and upvote every further reference to it. Reddit is a meme website, it is a site of imitation.

I couldn't believe the popularity of posts such as "X 7/10... X with rice 10/10". They are ridiculous and irrelevant to any conversation. Despite this, they were sometimes the most upvoted. But I guess it is reddit's nature and necessity to self-reference. It's kind of a recognition they need, a sense of identity.
